title: Enhanced Ground Truth for Cross-Repo Impact Analysis
description: Schema for defining verifiable, structured ground truths for benchmarking LLMs on cross-repository breaking change impact analysis. Replaces prose-based ground truths with analytically decomposed facts that enable automated scoring without LLM judges.

id.description: Unique question identifier matching the question.json id (e.g. MIXED_TC007, OBS_TC001)

question.description: The full question text, copied from question.json for self-containedness

change.description: The source of the breaking change — what changed, where, and the before/after state. This anchors the entire ground truth.

module.description: Fully qualified module/type/field being changed (e.g. metav1.ObjectMeta.Labels, cache.SharedInformer)

source_repo.description: Repository where the change originates (e.g. kubernetes, prometheus)

source_file.description: File path within the source repo where the module is defined (e.g. staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1/types.go)

before.description: The original signature/definition before the change (e.g. Labels map[string]string)

after.description: The new signature/definition after the change (e.g. Labels LabelMap)

description.description: Human-readable summary of what the change does and why it breaks downstream code

breaking_patterns.description: Finite enumerable set of code patterns that break due to this change. Each impacted file maps to one or more of these pattern IDs. Keeping this as a top-level lookup avoids repetition in impacted_files.

id.description: Short machine-friendly identifier for this pattern (e.g. direct_index_read, range_iteration). Used as a foreign key in impacted_files.

example.description: Minimal Go code snippet demonstrating the pattern (e.g. obj.Labels[key])

why_breaks.description: Explanation of why this pattern breaks after the change

impacted_files.description: Every file across the target repos that WILL break due to this change. Each entry is a verifiable fact — the code_evidence can be confirmed via grep/AST. This is the core of the ground truth.

repo.description: Repository name as it appears in dataset/Kubecluster/ (e.g. argo-cd, cert-manager)

file.description: File path relative to the repo root (e.g. applicationset/controllers/applicationset_controller.go)

breaking_patterns.description: List of breaking_pattern IDs that apply to this file. A file can match multiple patterns (e.g. both direct_index_read and direct_index_write).

code_evidence.description: Actual code snippets from this file that will break. Each should be greppable in the source. Multiple snippets if the file has multiple breaking usages.

severity.description: Impact severity. compile_error = won't compile; runtime_behavior_change = compiles but behaves differently; test_failure = compiles and runs but tests fail.

suggested_fix.description: What the code should be changed to after the breaking change. Enables scoring whether a model understood the required fix, not just the location.

false_positives.description: Files that LOOK relevant (mention Labels, import ObjectMeta, etc.) but DO NOT actually break. Models that list these should be penalized for hallucination. Models that correctly omit these should be rewarded.

file.description: File path relative to repo root

why_not_affected.description: Explanation of why this file does NOT break despite appearing relevant (e.g. accesses labels through an abstraction layer, only uses Annotations not Labels, etc.)

impact_summary.description: Aggregate counts for quick validation and high-level scoring. These should be derivable from impacted_files but are pre-computed for convenience.

by_pattern.description: Count of impacted files per breaking_pattern ID (e.g. { direct_index_write: 6, range_iteration: 3 })

by_severity.description: Count of impacted files per severity level (e.g. { compile_error: 14 })
